question.question: Triangle $ABC$ has $AB = 5\,\text{cm}$, $AC = 4\,\text{cm}$, and area $8\,\text{cm}^2$. Given that $\theta = \angle BAC$ is acute, find $\theta$ using the area formula.
question.referenceAnswer: Using $\text{area} = \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times AC \times \sin \theta$: $8 = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4 \times \sin \theta$, so $\sin \theta = \frac{4}{5}$. Since $\theta$ is acute, $\theta = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) \approx 53.1^\circ$.
question.evidence: Area of $\triangle ABC = \frac{1}{2} \times AB \times AC \times \sin A$; $8 = \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 4 \times \sin \theta$; $\sin \theta = \frac{4}{5}$; $\theta = 53.130^\circ$ or $180^\circ - 53.130^\circ$ (reject); $= 53.1^\circ$
